answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock stake in a cryptographic vault before climbing to a governance summit. Registering identities requires a non-refundable stake burning fee proportional to O(k^2.5), imposing superlinear cost scaling on attackers. A rogue entity trying to seed identities like a walnut grove finds its capital shattered against this reef of compounding economic friction, rendering multi-agent swarms mathematically unviable.
